patients.summary: Retired math teacher with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3, BPH after TURP and untreated Parkinson disease who joins in 2020. From 2023 he develops normal pressure hydrocephalus and Parkinson disease dementia, then Mobitz I block, a chronic subdural hematoma, and in July 2026 cardiac tamponade, all through outside care.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
70 y/o M here to establish, with wife. Prior PCP retiring.

HPI: Feels well. Has had BP and sugar issues for many years, managed by his old doctor, says numbers have been 'pretty steady.' Doesn't check sugar at home more than once in a while. Kidney function has been 'a little low' for a few years, he was told stage 3, never saw a kidney doctor. Parkinson's diagnosed last year by a neurologist after he noticed some stiffness, told it was mild and they'd hold off on medicine; hasn't gone back. Prostate surgery in 2018 helped his stream a lot; still on tamsulosin at night, gets up once.

PMH: HTN, T2DM, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3a, BPH, Parkinson disease (mild, untreated).
PSH: L inguinal hernia repair 2010, TURP 2018, bilateral cataract surgery with lens implants 2019.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID with meals, lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 qhs, tamsulosin 0.4 qhs.
Allergies: none to medications.
FHx: father CAD, heart attack at 76, died at 78. Mother T2DM and Lewy body dementia, died at 84. Sister (70) and son (45) both with HTN.
SHx: Married, lives with wife in Easthampton. Retired high school math teacher. Quit cigarettes about 20 yrs ago, roughly 20 pack-years. A glass or two of wine a week.

ROS: no chest pain, SOB, edema. No falls. Memory fine per wife. Bowels normal.

Exam: BP and vitals per flowsheet. Pleasant, conversational, good historian. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament felt throughout, DP pulses 2+. Neuro: mild cogwheeling R wrist, no rest tremor today, gait normal speed with normal arm swing.

A/P:
1. HTN - at goal on lisinopril 20.
2. T2DM - check A1c, UACR. Continue metformin.
3. CKD 3a - BMP today, avoid NSAIDs reviewed.
4. Hyperlipidemia - lipids today, continue atorvastatin.
5. BPH s/p TURP - stable on tamsulosin.
6. Parkinson disease, mild - follows neuro elsewhere in the past; he declines a referral for now, will revisit.
7. HM - HCV screen today. Records request to old office for colonoscopy and vaccine history. Flu shot in the fall.
RTC 3-4 months.

- Atorvastatin 40 for many years.
- Creatinine mildly elevated since 2017, labeled CKD stage 3a; urine microalbumin normal.
- Neurology consult 5/2019 (outside group): mild rigidity right arm, mild bradykinesia, impression early Parkinson disease, observation without medication.
- Colonoscopy 2015: normal to the terminal ileum, no further screening advised given age at next interval.
- Tdap 4/2016. Pneumococcal and shingles vaccines not documented.
- Urology: TURP 2018, continued tamsulosin.
Abstracted to chart.

orders.reason: progressive gait change, cognitive change, urinary urgency, falls

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife, who asked for this visit.
HPI: Since around January she has noticed he walks slower and his feet seem to stick, takes small steps. Fell twice in the last month - once in the garage, once getting up from the couch - no head strike, no LOC, no injury. Repeating himself, misplacing things. Has to rush to the bathroom and has wet himself a few times. He minimizes all of it, 'just getting old.'
Exam: vitals ok. Alert, oriented, but slow to answer. Heart regular, lungs clear. Gait: wide, slow, short steps, feet barely clear the floor, turns in several steps. Rigidity both legs more than arms. No focal weakness.
A/P: Subacute gait decline with cognitive change and urgency in a man with known mild PD. This is more than his PD has looked like. Neurology referral, asked for a prompt slot. Home safety reviewed - remove throw rugs, night lights, grab bar. Labs today. Wife to call with any further fall.

documents.author: PCP

History of mild Parkinson disease (outside neurology 2019, untreated), HTN, T2DM, CKD 3a, BPH s/p TURP. Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, tamsulosin 0.4. NKDA. Thank you for seeing him.

events.reason: gait difficulty, memory problems, urinary urgency

reports.text: Technique: axial non-contrast images of the head. Findings: The lateral and third ventricles are enlarged. Cortical sulci show minimal atrophy, less than expected for the ventricular size. No hemorrhage, mass or extra-axial collection. No acute infarct. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Calvarium intact. Bilateral lens implants.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged ventricles with minimal cortical atrophy.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient neurology consultation, date of service 7/17/2023.

Reason for referral: gait decline, memory, bladder.

Mr. Holt is a 72-year-old right-handed retired teacher, seen with his wife. Over roughly six months he has had worsening walking, forgetfulness and urinary urgency with occasional incontinence. His wife describes a shuffle and two falls in the past month. He asks the same questions more than once in a conversation.

History: mild Parkinson disease diagnosed 2019, never treated. HTN, T2DM, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3, BPH after TURP 2018. Cataract surgery both eyes 2019, L hernia repair 2010.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother had Lewy body dementia and diabetes; father coronary disease.
Social: former smoker (20 pack-years, quit ~20 years), minimal alcohol.

Examination: Strength full in all four limbs. Tone increased in both lower extremities. Gait broad-based with short, magnetic steps; unable to walk heel-to-toe. 

CT head (today): enlarged ventricles, only minimal cortical atrophy.

Impression: Gait apraxia, cognitive slowing and urge incontinence with ventriculomegaly out of proportion to atrophy - normal pressure hydrocephalus. Background Parkinson disease.

Plan: Follow-up in 3 months with repeat imaging.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Neurology visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, this is Gene's wife. The neurologist said he has fluid on the brain, normal pressure something. Did you get the report? What does it mean for him? We are worried.

documents.title: RE: Neurology visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, I have the letter and the CT. It's called normal pressure hydrocephalus - the fluid spaces in the brain are larger than they should be, and that can affect walking, memory and the bladder, which fits what you've been seeing. The neurologist plans to see him again in about 3 months with another scan. Happy to go over it in person at his September visit or sooner if you'd like.

documents.author: PCP

AWV, with wife.
Interval: neurology 7/17 - NPH on CT, follow-up with repeat scan in October.
HRA: no falls since June after rugs came up and grab bar went in. Wife now does finances and drives most of the time. Still dresses and bathes himself. Urgency persists, uses pads at night.
Cognitive screen not repeated today, neurology following. PHQ-2 1.
Advance directive: none. Discussed again with both - naming a proxy now while he can choose. Form given; wife to bring it back.
Vaccines: flu and updated covid today. RSV vaccine reviewed, he qualifies; pharmacy.
Exam: heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet intact. Gait wide-based, short steps, slow turns. Leg rigidity.
A/P: NPH and PD - per neurology. HTN, DM, CKD 3a, HLD - annual labs. Fall precautions continue. RTC 4 months.

documents.author: PCP

reports.text: Comparison 7/17/2023. Non-contrast axial images. The ventricles remain enlarged, similar to the prior study. Sulci are not widened; no cortical atrophy is seen. No hemorrhage, mass effect or extra-axial fluid. No acute territorial infarct.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged ventricles, unchanged. No cortical atrophy.

Neurology follow-up, seen 10/18/2023, accompanied by wife.

Seen in July for gait change. Known Parkinson disease and normal pressure hydrocephalus. Walking has kept getting harder since early this year; he says his feet feel glued to the floor. His wife finds him more forgetful and he sometimes does not reach the toilet in time.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg. NKDA.

Exam: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; fundi without papilledema. Gait broad-based and magnetic with hesitation on starting.

Urinalysis today unremarkable.
Repeat non-contrast CT head: ventricles enlarged as before, no cortical atrophy.

Impression: NPH with gait-predominant picture, background PD.
Plan: Return in about 3 months.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Neurology return visit 1/8/2024.

Mr. Holt, 73, with Parkinson disease and NPH, last seen here in July and October for gait and bladder symptoms. His wife comes with him today mainly about memory. Over the past year he has steadily lost ground: he gets turned around driving to places he has known for decades, and she has taken over the bills because he could no longer keep them straight - this from a man who taught algebra. At night he talks and moves about as if acting out dreams. He mentions seeing small animals in the house; she sees nothing there.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin; tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime. NKDA.
Family history notable for maternal Lewy body dementia.

BP 142/88.
Exam: Rest tremor present. Bradykinesia on finger and foot tapping. MMSE 24/30, points lost mainly on attention and visuospatial items.

Labs today: fasting glucose 138, HbA1c 7.2%, total cholesterol 185.

Assessment: Cognitive decline with visual hallucinations and dream enactment developing on a background of established Parkinson disease - Parkinson disease dementia. NPH as previously described.

Copy to primary care.

reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain without contrast. Mild generalized volume loss. Ventricles prominent. No restricted diffusion to suggest acute infarct. No significant white matter signal abnormality. No mass, hemorrhage or extra-axial collection. Flow voids preserved.
reports.conclusion: Mild generalized atrophy. No acute infarct or significant white matter disease.

documents.title: Geriatrics consultation
documents.author: geriatrics
documents.body:
Geriatric medicine consultation, 7/16/2024.

73-year-old man with Parkinson disease, NPH and Parkinson disease dementia (diagnosed by neurology in January), referred by his primary care physician. His daughter gives most of the history. Over the last year his confusion and memory come and go across the day, with stretches where he is entirely himself. He still describes small animals in the house. He reports his hands have become stiffer and more tremulous over about six months.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, atenolol 25 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Shuffling gait. Bradykinesia. Resting tremor. MMSE 24/30, deficits in attention and visuospatial function. No focal neurologic deficit and nothing to suggest stroke.

Labs: CBC normal. Electrolytes normal. Fasting glucose 148. HbA1c 7.2%. TSH and B12 normal.
MRI brain: mild generalized atrophy; no acute infarct or significant white matter disease.

Assessment: Fluctuating cognition and visual hallucinations consistent with his Parkinson disease dementia; no reversible metabolic contributor found; no vascular burden on MRI.

Family given caregiver resources. Return as needed.

documents.title: Geriatrics letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I received the geriatrics consultation. Good news that the blood tests and MRI did not show anything else contributing. Please use the caregiver resources they gave you, and call us anytime things change at home.

Will get him a prompt cardiology appointment to look at rhythm given slow pulse on atenolol. Rise slowly, sit if lightheaded, ED for any fainting or chest pain. Daughter agrees.

conditions.label: Mobitz type I second-degree AV block

reports.text: Sinus rhythm with progressive lengthening of the PR interval over successive beats, ending in a P wave that is not conducted; the cycle then repeats. Narrow QRS. No acute ST changes.
reports.conclusion: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz type I.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology consultation, 7/7/2025.

Referred for two weeks of intermittent lightheadedness. Background Parkinson disease, NPH and dementia; daughter present. He denies chest pain, palpitations or fainting.

Medications: metformin, lisinopril, atenolol 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg qhs, tamsulosin 0.4 mg qhs. NKDA.

BP 130/80, HR 58, RR 16. Pulse irregular. Heart sounds normal, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
Electrolytes normal.
ECG: PR lengthens beat to beat until one P wave fails to conduct, then the sequence restarts.

Impression: Mobitz type I second-degree AV block, likely aggravated by beta-blockade; lightheadedness may relate.

Plan: Stop atenolol. No indication for pacing at this time. Return or seek care for syncope or worsening dizziness. Blood pressure follow-up with primary care.

documents.title: Medication change from cardiology
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called wife after cardiology letter arrived. Atenolol stopped 7/7 - she confirms he has not taken it since. Med list updated. Asked her to keep logging BP and pulse and send in a week or two. Problem list updated with the heart block.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily in the morning

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV + BP. Wife present.
Cardiology 7/7: Mobitz I block; atenolol stopped. Lightheaded spells have not recurred per wife. Home BPs since then mostly 140s-150s/80s-90s; above goal again today.
Function: needs help bathing and dressing some days, no falls this year. Wife is managing but tired; daughter visits monthly.
PHQ-2 1.
Advance directive: none on file. Third conversation - wife will sit down with him and the children. Form given again.
Vaccines: flu and covid today.
Exam: heart irregular at times, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Feet intact. Tremor and shuffle unchanged.
A/P:
1. HTN off beta-blocker - add HCTZ 12.5 mg daily (avoiding AV-nodal agents). BMP in 3 weeks at nurse visit.
2. Mobitz I - per cardiology; avoid beta-blockers and non-DHP CCBs.
3. DM, CKD 3a, HLD - annual labs.
4. PD dementia, NPH - stable, family support.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: BP recheck 3 weeks after starting HCTZ. Reading per flowsheet, improved. No dizziness per wife. BMP drawn. PCP notified.

documents.title: Blood pressure and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: BP was much better yesterday and sodium and potassium are fine on the new water pill. Kidney numbers about the same as September. Stay on it.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination

documents.body: Exam 11/10/2025. Patient cooperative with wife's help. VA 20/40 OU. IOLs stable. No diabetic retinopathy. Recall 1 year. Allergies: NKDA.

events.reason: headache, confusion, difficulty walking after a fall

reports.text: Non-contrast CT of the head. A crescent-shaped extra-axial collection along the left cerebral convexity is hyperdense relative to brain. It exerts mass effect with rightward midline shift. Ventricles enlarged as on prior imaging. No intraparenchymal hemorrhage. No skull fracture.
reports.conclusion: Left convexity subdural hematoma with midline shift.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, 1/15/2026.

CC: headache, confusion, trouble walking.

75-year-old man with NPH and Parkinson disease dementia, prior falls and day-to-day cognitive swings, brought by his daughter. Two weeks of headache that keeps getting worse, on-and-off confusion and more trouble walking; over the last few days he has been sleepier than usual. He fell about three weeks ago without passing out and did not see anyone for it.

PMH: NPH, PD dementia, Parkinson disease, Mobitz I AV block, HTN, T2DM, hyperlipidemia, CKD 3, BPH s/p TURP.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, metformin 1000 mg BID, tamsulosin 0.4 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg. No anticoagulant or antiplatelet. NKDA.

BP 145/85, HR 78, RR 16.
Exam: awake, disoriented to time. Mild weakness on the right side. Right pupil reacts sluggishly.

CT head: crescent-shaped hyperdense collection over the left convexity with midline shift.
CBC, BMP and INR sent.

Impression: Chronic subdural hematoma, left.
Neurosurgery consulted. Admitted to neurosurgical service.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body:
Admitted 1/15/2026, discharged 1/20/2026.

Diagnosis: Left chronic subdural hematoma after a fall.

Hospital course: 75M with NPH, Parkinson disease dementia and Mobitz I block presented with two weeks of headache, fluctuating confusion and gait decline about three weeks after a fall, with mild right-sided weakness. CT showed a left convexity chronic subdural hematoma with midline shift. Taken for burr-hole evacuation on 1/16 without complication. Headache settled; confusion improved toward his baseline per daughter. Walking at his usual pace at discharge.

Discharge medications (unchanged from home): lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime, tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: neurosurgery clinic in about 5 weeks with CT head; primary care in 2-4 weeks. Return for new headache, worsening confusion, weakness or another fall.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with daughter. Home since 1/20. Headache gone. Eating and sleeping. Taking his usual five meds, no new ones. Incision clean and dry. Neurosurgery follow-up booked late February. Scheduled PCP visit 2/13. Reviewed reasons to call 911.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Hospital follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With daughter and wife.
Admitted 1/15-1/20 for L chronic SDH about 3 weeks after an unwitnessed fall; burr-hole evacuation 1/16. Discharge summary reviewed.
Since home: no headache. Daughter says his thinking is back to how it was before the fall - good mornings, foggier afternoons. Walking at his usual shuffle. No further falls. Taking the same five medications.
Exam: alert, oriented to person and place. Scalp incision healed. Pupils equal and reactive. Strength symmetric, right side now equal to left. Rest tremor, shuffling gait as at baseline. Heart irregular at times, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P:
1. Chronic SDH s/p evacuation - recovered to baseline. Neurosurgery f/u with CT 2/24. No antiplatelets.
2. Falls - home safety revisited.
3. HTN - acceptable on lisinopril + HCTZ.
4. CKD - creatinine has climbed over the past year (about 1.6 last fall and in the hospital); recheck today.

Addendum 4:30 pm: creatinine 1.9 today, eGFR now under 45 - CKD restaged 3b. Same medications; recheck in 3 months.
5. DM - A1c today.
6. PD dementia, NPH, Mobitz I - unchanged.
Advance directive: still none on file - urged the family again given the hospitalization.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Results from Friday: blood count normal, sodium and potassium normal. Kidney function is lower than last fall - creatinine 1.9 - so I have changed the stage of his kidney disease on his chart to 3b. We will keep his medicines the same and recheck in a few months. A1c about the same. Please keep him off ibuprofen and naproxen.

reports.text: Comparison 1/15/2026. Postoperative change from a left burr hole. The left convexity subdural collection is much smaller. No midline shift. No new hemorrhage. Ventricles enlarged as before.
reports.conclusion: Much smaller left subdural collection after evacuation; midline shift resolved.

documents.title: Neurosurgery follow-up
documents.author: neurosurgery
documents.body: Neurosurgery clinic, 2/24/2026. Five weeks after left burr-hole evacuation of a chronic subdural hematoma. Family reports he is back to his baseline. Incision well healed. Strength equal both sides. CT today: much smaller collection, no midline shift. No further imaging planned unless new symptoms. Discharged from neurosurgery follow-up. NKDA.

documents.body: Pharmacy request for lisinopril 20 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, 90 days x 3. Seen 2/13. Sent.

reports.text: Sinus P waves at a regular rate. Every third P wave is not followed by a QRS (3:2 conduction). On this strip the PR of conducted beats does not clearly lengthen before the blocked beat. Narrow QRS. Repeat tracing after vagal maneuvers: some P waves that were previously blocked now conduct, with a long PR interval.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, 4/8/2026.

CC: dizziness, palpitations.

75-year-old man with known Mobitz I second-degree AV block, PD dementia, NPH and recent SDH evacuation, back with several weeks of intermittent dizziness and a fluttering feeling in the chest. No chest pain, shortness of breath or fainting.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime. No AV-nodal blocking drugs. NKDA.

BP 130/80, HR 56, RR 16.
Irregular pulse. Lungs clear. No edema.

ECG: second-degree AV block, every third P wave non-conducted; PR of conducted beats not clearly progressive on this tracing. After vagal maneuvers, some previously blocked P waves conducted with a prolonged PR.
BMP and CBC unremarkable.

Impression: Second-degree AV block in a patient with known type I block; symptoms intermittent, hemodynamically stable.
Disposition: discharged home with family. Outpatient cardiology follow-up advised. Return for fainting, chest pain or worsening dizziness.

documents.title: ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is his daughter. Dad was in the ER Wednesday night for dizzy spells, they said his heart block was acting up and sent him home and told us to see cardiology. Should we call cardiology ourselves?

documents.title: RE: ER visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know - I have the ER record. Yes, please call the cardiology office he saw last July and ask for a follow-up about the ER visit. If he faints, has chest pain or the dizziness gets worse, go straight back to the ER.

documents.title: Metformin refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request for metformin 1000 mg BID, 90 days. Sent with 1 refill; note to family to book a follow-up visit.

reports.text: Low-voltage QRS complexes in limb and precordial leads. Beat-to-beat alternation of QRS amplitude (electrical alternans).

Limited bedside study. Large circumferential pericardial effusion. Right ventricular diastolic collapse and right atrial collapse. Dilated inferior vena cava without respiratory variation. Left ventricular systolic function grossly preserved.
reports.conclusion: Large pericardial effusion with echocardiographic tamponade.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Emergency department, 7/11/2026.

CC: found unresponsive.

75-year-old man with Parkinson disease, PD dementia, NPH and prior AV block, found unresponsive at home by a neighbor. He cannot give a history. The neighbor says he had complained on and off of chest pain over the past week.

Meds (per pharmacy list): lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime. NKDA.

Afebrile. BP 90/60, HR 52, RR 22.
Exam: jugular veins distended, heart sounds distant, extremities cold.

Labs: Hgb 13.2, WBC 7.8, platelets 210. Creatinine 2.1 (baseline 1.9), BUN 44, K 4.5. Troponin I elevated.
ECG: low-voltage QRS, electrical alternans.
Bedside echo: large pericardial effusion with tamponade physiology.

His son arrived shortly after; he does not know what his father would want regarding invasive procedures and there is no advance directive on file. Risks and benefits of drainage discussed with the son, who agreed to proceed.

Impression: Cardiac tamponade.
Course: Cardiology performed emergent subxiphoid pericardiocentesis in the ED, 650 mL removed, drain left in place, blood pressure improved after drainage. Admitted to cardiology step-down.

reports.text: Follow-up study after pericardial drain removal. Trace residual pericardial fluid. No chamber collapse. Normal inferior vena cava size with respiratory variation. Left ventricular systolic function normal.
reports.conclusion: Trace residual pericardial effusion, no tamponade.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Admitted 7/11/2026, discharged 7/16/2026.

Diagnosis: Cardiac tamponade from a large pericardial effusion; cause not established.

Course: Found unresponsive at home after a week of intermittent chest pain; hypotensive with JVD, distant heart sounds and electrical alternans; echo with large effusion and tamponade. Emergent subxiphoid pericardiocentesis in the ED drained 650 mL; consent from his son. Troponin I elevated on arrival and trended down after drainage. Drain removed after 48 hours. Repeat echo 7/13: trace residual fluid, no tamponade. Pericardial fluid culture: no growth. Cytology: no malignant cells. Mental status returned to his baseline per family.

Discharge medications (unchanged): lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime, tamsulosin 0.4 mg at bedtime.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: cardiology clinic in about 4 weeks with echo. Primary care after discharge. Family encouraged to complete a health care proxy.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called son after discharge summary received. Home since 7/16. No chest pain or shortness of breath reported. Same five medications. Cardiology appointment 8/12 with echo. Family will call to set up a primary care visit after that. Reminded about the health care proxy form.

reports.text: Complete study. No pericardial effusion. Normal left ventricular size and systolic function. Normal right ventricular size and function. No significant valvular disease. Normal inferior vena cava with respiratory variation.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Cardiology clinic, 8/12/2026, with his son. One month after pericardiocentesis for tamponade (650 mL, culture and cytology negative, cause not established). No chest pain or breathlessness per family. Known Mobitz I block.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 40 mg, tamsulosin 0.4 mg. NKDA.

Echo today: no pericardial effusion.

Plan: No further echo unless symptoms recur. Continue to avoid AV-nodal blockers. Return as needed.
